narrative_markdown:
## Today's Forecast

Isolated afternoon showers and thunderstorms are expected with a high of 31°C / 87°F and a low of 20°C / 68°F. Overcast skies early become mostly cloudy by midday and evening. Peak wind gusts ashore will reach 40 km/h (22 kt), with wind west-southwesterly by midday, turning west-northwest into the evening. Thunder possible, peaking this evening. Peak UV index is 9.2 today. Model estimated air quality is AQI 72, while ground stations report up to AQI 62 at Dunga Beach. As of 06:01, reports through 04:00: no rain; no thunder; high so far 22°C / 72°F; low so far 19°C / 66°F; peak sustained 7 km/h; sky mostly clear.

## Extended Outlook

Temperatures and winds much the same through Wednesday, with showers and thunderstorms likely each day. Skies mostly cloudy throughout. Wednesday's call: rain, 100%, with all four models wet; highs around 30 °C. At this lead ICON has the best record, right 73% of the time over 71 checks.

Further out, temperatures and winds much the same through Sunday, with rain and thunderstorms likely Thursday, Friday and Saturday, and showers and thunderstorms possible Sunday. Thursday: all four models wet, highs 27 to 32 °C. Friday: all four models wet, the week's wettest day at 15 mm on average, highs around 28 °C. Saturday: all three models that reach it wet, highs 27 to 30 °C.

Only GFS, ECMWF and ICON reach past Friday. ICON is the wetter solution from Thursday to Friday; GFS, ECMWF and UKMO keep it drier. Sunday's call: rain, 100%, with both models wet; highs around 28 °C. At this lead ECMWF has the best record, right 77% of the time over 67 checks.

## Severe Weather / Hazard Potential

Peak CAPE values today reach 580 J/kg for GFS, 1300 J/kg for ECMWF, 1630 J/kg for ICON, 1810 J/kg for Best Match, and 4460 J/kg for UKMO. Above the thunderstorm threshold, any thunderstorm brings the hazard of sudden gusts well above the forecast wind. The local meteorological service bulletin carries no severe weather warning.

## Winam Gulf — Conditions for Boaters

Winds on the Winam Gulf run overnight at 7 km/h (4 kt) gusting 11 km/h (6 kt), then southwesterly by midday at 8 km/h (4 kt) gusting 20 km/h (11 kt), then northwesterly into the evening at 12 km/h (6 kt) gusting 23 km/h (13 kt); peak gust 30 km/h (16 kt). Where thunderstorms are possible, they bring the hazard of sudden gusts well above forecast winds.

## Detailed Discussion

### Synoptic Overview

Across roughly 2,600 km, pressure is lowest toward the north (1007 hPa) and highest toward the southeast (1015 hPa) — an 8 hPa spread, a moderate large-scale gradient. Pressure is also falling toward the south — a large-scale feature building in that direction, though this sampling cannot say how fast or whether it will reach here. Pressure overhead is near-steady. Across 5 points, today's mean sea-level pressure sits between 1012.7 and 1014.8 hPa; near-steady over three days (+0.5 hPa). Pressure trend shows +1.5 hPa, with lowest pressure lying toward the north.

### Forecaster Confidence Notes

At Day+0, no model is meaningfully better than the others here yet, while GFS has the best rain record at 77% over the last 30 checks. Today's call of 3.6 mm sits within the model range from 0.2 mm (UKMO) to 12.6 mm (ICON). ICON sits on the wrong side of its bias record by over-forecasting overnight lows with 21.6°C. Kenya Meteorological Department (KMD) predicts a high of 30.0°C and low of 21.0°C, agreeing with the call. Data sufficiency represents a settled picture with 55 checks for the least-covered model.
